'''Maciej Lewenstein''' (born September 21, 1955) is a Polish theoretical physicist, currently working as an [[Catalan Institution for Research and Advanced Studies|ICREA]] research professor<ref name="icrea">{{cite web |url=https://www.icrea.cat/community/icreas/17467/maciej-andrzej-lewenstein/ |title=Maciej Lewenstein, ICREA |website=ICREA Community |access-date=27 August 2026}}</ref> at [[ICFO – The Institute of Photonic Sciences]]<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.icfo.eu/about-icfo/people/directory/?id=9 |title=Prof. Dr. Maciej Lewenstein |website=icfo.eu |access-date=18 January 2023}}</ref> in [[Castelldefels]] near [[Barcelona]].

== Education ==
Maciej Lewenstein was born on 21 September 1955 in [[Warsaw]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://pan.pl/czlonkowie/maciej-lewenstein/ |title=Maciej Lewenstein |publisher=Polish Academy of Sciences |access-date=27 August 2026}}</ref> He graduated from the Institute for Theoretical Physics (ITP) at the [[University of Warsaw]] in 1978, completing his diploma thesis on the superradiance phenomenon under the supervision of [[Kazimierz Rzążewski]]. After working for one year as a scientific assistant at the ITP, he joined the newly formed Centre for Theoretical Physics of the [[Polish Academy of Sciences]] (CFT) in Warsaw in 1979, which was established by [[Iwo Białynicki-Birula]]. At the CFT, he began his PhD studies on the applications of functional integration methods in [[quantum optics]] with Rzążewski. In 1981, he received a [[German Academic Exchange Service|DAAD]] scholarship to study at the [[University of Duisburg-Essen|University of Essen]]. There, he completed his doctoral thesis under the joint supervision of Fritz Haake in 1983, graduating [[summa cum laude]] and receiving the Prize of the University.<ref name="fnp">{{cite web |url=https://fnp.org.pl |title=Prof. Maciej Lewenstein – Biography |publisher=Foundation for Polish Science |access-date=27 August 2026}}</ref>

From 1984 to 1986, he worked as a postdoctoral researcher at the University of Essen alongside Haake, focusing on the statistical physics of disordered systems. After returning to Poland and becoming a faculty member at the CFT, he completed his [[Habilitation|habilitation]] in 1986 at the Institute of Physics of the [[Polish Academy of Sciences]] with a thesis on [[cavity quantum electrodynamics]] and intense laser–matter interactions.<ref name="fnp" />

== Research career ==
After completing his habilitation, he spent three years as a research associate with the Nobel laureate [[Roy J. Glauber]] at [[Harvard University]]. In the early 1990s, he continued to expand his collaborations on the [[quantum optics]] of [[dielectric]] media and [[cavity quantum electrodynamics]] with Glauber, as well as with [[Thomas W. Mossberg]]. He was also an associate member of the Institute for Social Studies at the University of Warsaw (ISS), where he developed collaborations with Andrzej Nowak and Bibb Latané.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Lewenstein |first1=Maciej |last2=Nowak |first2=Andrzej |last3=Latané |first3=Bibb |title=Statistical mechanics of social impact |journal=Physical Review A |volume=45 |issue=2 |pages=763–768 |date=1 January 1992 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevA.45.763}}</ref> In 1992, he spent a six-month sabbatical at the Service des Photons, Atomes et Molécules (SPAM) of the [[Commissariat à l'énergie atomique et aux énergies alternatives|Commissariat à l'énergie atomique]] (CEA) in Saclay. There, he began his research into the foundations of attosecond physics and high harmonic generation alongside [[Anne L'Huillier]] (Nobel 2023). In 1993, he spent a year as a visiting fellow at [[JILA]] (Joint Institute for Laboratory Astrophysics) in Boulder, Colorado, where he continued his work on attosecond physics while initiating interests in the physics of ultracold atoms and quantum information, co-running a joint seminar on [[Bose–Einstein condensate|Bose–Einstein condensation]] with [[Peter Zoller]] and [[Eric Allin Cornell]] (Nobel 2001). In 1994, he spent six months at the [[Institute for Theoretical Atomic and Molecular Physics]] at the [[Harvard–Smithsonian Center for Astrophysics]], continuing his studies of ultracold gases with Glauber.<ref name="icrea" /><ref name="Lamb">{{cite web |url=https://www.lambaward.com/bio/maclej-lewenstein |title=Maciej Lewenstein CV, Lamb Award |publisher=Lamb Award |access-date=27 August 2026}}</ref>

In 1995, he joined the faculty of SPAM at the CEA in Saclay, where he spent three and a half years dividing his research between the physics of ultraintense laser–matter interactions, attosecond physics, the physics of ultracold gases, and [[quantum information]]. In 1998, he became a full professor at [[Leibniz University Hannover]], remaining there until 2005. In 2005, he moved to Spain as an ICREA research professor to lead the quantum optics theory group at [[ICFO – The Institute of Photonic Sciences|ICFO – the Institute of Photonic Sciences]] in [[Castelldefels]].<ref name="icrea" /><ref name="Lamb" />

== Selected publications ==
* ''Polish Jazz Recordings and Beyond'' – Maciej Lewenstein, Warszawska Firma Wydawnicza (2015).<ref>{{cite book |last=Lewenstein |first=Maciej |title=Polish Jazz Recordings and Beyond |publisher=Warszawska Firma Wydawnicza |year=2014 |isbn=9788380117440 |location=Warsaw}}</ref>
* ''Ultracold Atoms in Optical Lattices: Simulating Quantum Many-Body Systems'' – Maciej Lewenstein, Anna Sanpera, and Verónica Ahufinger, Oxford University Press (2012).<ref>{{cite book |last1=Lewenstein |first1=Maciej |last2=Sanpera |first2=Anna |last3=Ahufinger |first3=Verónica |title=Ultracold Atoms in Optical Lattices: Simulating Quantum Many-Body Systems |publisher=Oxford University Press |year=2012 |isbn=9780199573127 |doi=10.1093/acprof:oso/9780199573127.001.0001}}</ref>

== Community service ==
He served as a division associate editor of [[Physical Review Letters]] from 1997<ref>{{cite web |url=https://aps.org |title=Physical Review Letters, vol. 79, no. 6 (Table of Contents) |website=APS Journals |publisher=[[American Physical Society]] |date=11 August 1997 |access-date=27 August 2026}}</ref> to 2003.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://aps.org |title=Physical Review Letters, vol. 90, no. 25 (Table of Contents) |website=APS Journals |publisher=[[American Physical Society]] |date=27 June 2003 |access-date=27 August 2026}}</ref> He has been a member of the editorial boards of ''Open Systems & Information Dynamics''<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.worldscientific.com/page/osid/editorial-board |title=Open Systems & Information Dynamics: Editorial Board |website=World Scientific |access-date=27 August 2026}}</ref> and ''[[Reports on Progress in Physics]]''<ref>{{cite web |url=https://publishingsupport.iopscience.iop.org/journals/reports-on-progress-in-physics/editorial-board/ |title=Reports on Progress in Physics: Editorial Board |website=IOPscience |access-date=27 August 2026}}</ref> as of 2026. He was also the chairman of the Quantum Optics and Photonics Division of the German Physical Society (DPG) from 2004 to 2006.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.dpg-physik.de/vereinigungen/fachlich/samop/fvq/geschichte-des-fachverbands |title=History of the Quantum Optics and Photonics (Q) Division |website=Deutsche Physikalische Gesellschaft |access-date=27 August 2026}}</ref>

== Awards and honors ==
* 2004 – Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]]<ref>{{cite web |url=https://aps.org |title=Maciej Lewenstein |website=Physics Magazine |publisher=[[American Physical Society]] |access-date=27 August 2026}}</ref>
* 2007 – [[Humboldt Research Award]]<ref name="fnp-laureat">{{cite web |url=https://archiwalna.fnp.org.pl/prof-maciej-lewenstein-laureat-nagrody-fnp-2011/ |title=Prof. Maciej Lewenstein – laureat Nagrody FNP 2011 |trans-title=Prof. Maciej Lewenstein – recipient of the Prize of the Foundation for Polish Science |language=pl |publisher=Foundation for Polish Science |access-date=27 August 2026}}</ref>
* 2010 – [[Hamburg Centre for Ultrafast Imaging#Awardees for the Hamburg Prize for Theoretical Physics|Hamburg Prize for Theoretical Physics]] (Hertz Foundation Award)<ref name="fnp-laureat" />
* 2011 – [[Prize of the Foundation for Polish Science]]<ref name="fnp-laureat" />
* 2013 – Gutenberg Research Award of the [[Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz]]<ref>{{cite web |url=https://uni-mainz.de |title=2013 – Prof. Maciej Lewenstein |publisher=Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz |access-date=27 August 2026}}</ref>
* 2013 – [[European Physical Society]] Quantum Electronics and Optics Division Prize for Fundamental Research<ref>{{cite web |url=http://epsdivisions.org |title=EPS-QEOD Prizes |website=Quantum Electronics and Optics Division |publisher=[[European Physical Society]] |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171122020410/http://epsdivisions.org |archive-date=22 November 2017 |access-date=27 August 2026}}</ref>
* 2016 – [[Spanish Royal Physics Society|RSEF]] Medal<ref>{{cite web |url=https://fbbva.es |title=The awards of the Spanish physics community champion science as a strategic activity with the power to advance social well-being |date=14 December 2017 |publisher=BBVA Foundation |access-date=27 August 2026}}</ref>
* 2016 – {{ill|Willis E. Lamb Award|de|}}<ref>{{cite web |url=https://lambaward.org |title=The Willis E. Lamb Award for Laser Science and Quantum Optics |website=lambaward.org |access-date=27 August 2026}}</ref>
* 2019 – Member of the [[Academia Europaea]]<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.ae-info.org/ae/Acad_Main/List_of_Members |title=Directory of Members |publisher=Academia Europaea |access-date=27 August 2026}}</ref>
